concerns.quote: buzzer/alarm in the deceased room had been removed/disabled due to a previous incident where the deceased had attempted to place the cord around her neck
observations were not recorded as to when they actually took place or what was observed.
deceased preferred to have her bedroom door left open but this did not form part of her care plan
other resident suspected to have been the assailant was a new referral to the home and that there was a lack of information on her admission
obvious signs of an injury to Edna's head in the form of the injury to her eye which resulted in bruising and swelling
no medical review was sought until an ambulance was called on 29/11/19 when the deceased became unresponsive

reports.title: Charles Evans: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: None of the Carers employed at Hibiscus House had any training in CPR
concerns.hazard: lack of CPR training among carers

concerns.quote: There was no Registered First Aider at the premises
There was no defibrillator on site
There was no emergency bell/alarm or telephone in the residents' dining room
Post inquest, the Coroner noted the CQC Inspection report for Hibiscus House Domiciliary Care Agency dated July 2019 which rated the facility as 'requiring improvement'
concerns.hazard: inadequate CQC follow-up on improvement plan

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of an emergency alarm or communication device that would allow residents to call for help. The earlier case concerns a disabled buzzer in a bedroom, while the later case notes no bell/alarm or telephone in the dining room.
